A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Quant VideoGen work. All 11 pages of each are readable, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 5, Table 1 and Figures 5–7 report original video-generation quality, compression, latency and sensitivity results.

after.justification: v4 retains the original empirical evaluations in Section 5, Table 1 and Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: Semantic-Aware Smoothing, Progressive Residual Quantization, centroid caching and fused dequantization remain unchanged in Section 4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MovieGen prompt suite and retain the same video-continuation, long-horizon generation and interactive-world scenarios. No dataset or tested scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 5 retain the same RTN, KIVI and QuaRot comparisons and BF16 references. Comparator membership and the restriction of QuaRot to KV-cache quantization are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same model configurations, 480p resolution, context and chunk lengths, fidelity and VBench metrics, and quantization settings. The first-chunk fidelity evaluation and long-generation evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The smoothing ablation, long-horizon quality analysis, memory decomposition, and sensitivity tests for quantization stages and group sizes are unchanged in Figures 5–7 and Sections 5.2–5.4.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are retained. For example, Table 1 reports QVG INT2 PSNR/compression of 28.716/6.94× for LongCat-Video and 29.174/7.05× for HY-WorldPlay in both versions; Section 5.3 retains latency overheads of 2.1%, 1.5% and 4.3%.

T1.justification: The KV-memory formula, quantization-error reasoning, smoothing definitions and progressive reconstruction equations are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free KV-cache compression, near-lossless quality, low latency overhead and enabling longer video generation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning context length and drift, smoothing of irregular activation distributions, and diminishing returns from additional quantization stages are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: v4 adds clickable project-website and GitHub repository links beneath the authors on page 1. Existing implementation and hardware details remain unchanged. This adds resource-access information; the PDFs do not establish the linked resources' contents or availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to video-generation and KV-cache-compression research are unchanged. Differences in bibliography back-reference page numbers reflect text reflow.

P1.justification: v4 adds a Resources line, author dagger markers and an Amazon-affiliation disclaimer, and updates date/version text. Scientific prose, terminology and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added first-page material causes limited text reflow across pages 1–4. Table 1 and Figures 1–7 retain their content, styling and placement; the methods/results pages 5–8 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The new page-1 website and GitHub links provide direct pointers to associated resources, modestly improving resource discoverability and reproducibility documentation. Scientific methods, evidence and conclusions are unchanged, and the supplied PDFs do not verify the linked resources' contents.
